## Workflow and responsibility

Cross Sections presents three hydraulic review regions: channel, left
descending-bank floodplain and right descending-bank floodplain. Polygon-derived
centerlines replace the rejected slice-midpoint/loess approximation. They are
reviewable geometric direction proxies, not measured hydraulic flow paths.
The feature record owns provisional method choices and scientific limits.

1. `mod_study_server()` mounts `cross_section_review_server()` with the linked
   Event selector and upstream revision signals. `load_flowline_points_review()`
   resolves exact saved Flowlines, Flowline Points and Hydro DEM inputs.
2. `cross_section_rem_queue()` queues saved Reaches from Flowline Points.
   `cross_section_rem_artifact()` calls `fluvgeo::detrend()` in a sequential
   background worker and publishes analytical/display REM GeoTIFFs, display
   limits and provenance. They persist across sessions with exact-input/recipe
   fingerprints and output hashes. Cross Sections reads those files immediately,
   preparing a missing Reach once when necessary. The inherited corridor can
   truncate evidence; the current metric project uses approximately 150 m.
3. The debounced worker calls `water_surface_extents()` with strictly ordered
   analyst levels. Original inundation retains holes; outer footprints fill
   holes without connecting disconnected parts.
4. `cross_section_regions()` partitions the outer footprint into three multipart
   parent regions with explicit component identities. `centerline::cnt_skeleton()`
   and `cnt_path()` produce per-component Voronoi skeletons and longitudinal raw
   routes. Douglas-Peucker/Chaikin proposals are retained only when simple and
   contained in their own component. Failures and rejected smoothing are explicit.
5. `cross_section_layout()` samples the saved measured Flowline, uses local
   tangents from the three polygon centerlines and constructs editable cut
   lines. An overbank uses the component touching its bank. A bank already on the
   outer boundary with no adjacent overbank is a zero-width floodplain side,
   distinct from missing/ambiguous direction evidence. A bank-to-centerline
   connector that leaves its polygon is replaced by the closest tested visible
   segment projection, preserving the source line and recording the adjustment.
   Channel cuts are perpendicular to the local channel-centerline tangent;
   width minimization and conflict-driven rotation are removed. One-sided GEOS
   rays propose full-coverage floodplain endpoints within the angular bound;
   tentative alternatives reduce contacts and angular departure before rank
   assignment. `cross_section_boundary_chains()` extracts directed
   shared edges and whole-channel bank arcs. `cross_section_order_anchors()`
   assigns outer targets in Seq order; `cross_section_refine_targets()` can repair
   infeasible proposals inside their ordered neighbor interval before freezing them.
   `cross_section_ordered_routes()` builds complete nonintersecting floodplain
   routes to those fixed targets, treating other channels and accepted legs as
   barriers. Extra vertices are unchecked by default. When enabled, constrained
   triangulation/graph routing and visibility shortcuts can add multiple vertices
   away from centerlines. Unsupported routes and channel contacts stay explicit.
   Explicit left_bank_vertex/right_bank_vertex retain channel identity with four
   or more vertices. No leg is shortened. The backend routing helper is
   `cross_section_deconflict.R`, with ordering in `cross_section_order.R`;
   tests include multi-bend obstacles, fixed endpoints and a wide confluence.
6. Original polygons, components, skeletons and raw/smoothed centerlines are
   separately reviewable. Polygons/centerlines appear first; candidate cut lines
   and permanent Seq numbers appear by default. Advanced settings and manual
   correction are collapsed. Boundary spacing, Chaikin passes and local tangent
   distance are distinct parameters. Direction review points identify shortened
   tangent windows, raw-centerline use and unavailable direction evidence
   separately from incomplete geometry. A session cache reuses skeletons and
   centerlines when only cut-line spacing or tangent distance changes.
7. Map clicks move an armed vertex after transformation from display to analysis
   CRS. `cross_section_layout_review()` refreshes orientation, endpoint fields,
   all-pair touches/crossings, self-crossings, endpoint gaps and outside length.
   With boundary chains supplied it also refreshes actual bank/outer rank and
   channel departure from perpendicular without moving geometry. Generated
   target evidence remains distinct from later manual edits.
   Deletion resequences mutable `Seq` and preserves remaining local candidate IDs.
   `cross_section_vertex_labels()` identifies banks and optional bends. Add/Remove
   floodplain bend changes the selected side, keeping banks/endpoints fixed and
   refreshing bank indices. Manual additions start at the leg midpoint.
8. Save draft re-resolves upstream evidence and `study_cross_section_store()`
   publishes an immutable schema-5 / method-v6 GeoPackage revision with PENDING protection,
   exact input/output hashes, and RDS/JSON indexes. Reopening restores controls
   and corrections only for matching inputs and method. Old loess drafts remain
   prior evidence and are not reused as polygon-centerline output.
   Changing controls can also reuse a saved draft for that exact settings set;
   readers verify the same lineage/output hashes before bypassing computation.

Raw input changes clear candidates before the 400 ms debounce expires. Workers
receive file paths and serializable inputs, validate their generation key, stop
before session cleanup and do not transfer raster external pointers. A failed
layout preserves valid inundation review. The analyst preview uses a fresh R
process and the isolated development backend library.

## Data objects and storage

| Object | Input/output | Representation and ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Flowline, Flowline Points, Hydro DEM | Exact saved Event/Reach inputs | Existing GeoPackage candidates and shared Stream GeoTIFF; resolved through the app store |
| Analytical/display REM | Persistent local preparation | Study-local cross-section-preparation/<input-recipe-hash>/rem.tif and display.tif; preparation.json/RDS retain source and output hashes; prepared by cross_section_rem_artifact, read by Cross Sections |
| Inundation and outer footprints | Selected levels and layout evidence | sf during review; saved source/outer polygon layers with draft |
| Three hydraulic regions | Channel, left and right floodplain parent polygons | `hydraulic_regions`, three MULTIPOLYGON rows including explicitly empty sides; `region_components` retains disconnected parts and local region_id |
| Skeletons and raw/smoothed centerlines | Independent polygon geometry and direction evidence | `centerline_skeleton`, `centerline_raw`, `centerline`; each row links to its source component and region role |
| Cut-line polylines and samples | Editable candidate geometry and local diagnostics | Standard `cross_section` and `side_support`; explicit bank indices, optional bend flags, leg status, rotation in degrees and tangent/raw-source flags; opaque local candidate IDs survive edits/reopen, Seq is mutable |
| Ordered edges and targets | Generated layout evidence | `boundary_chains` LINESTRINGs and `boundary_anchors` POINTs retain chain identity/role/orientation and candidate/Seq/side, planned boundary positions, status and explicit feature-CRS measure units. Whole-channel bank arcs check order across floodplain components. Actual section order flags are refreshed on edits/save. |
| Method and review evidence | Settings, source lineage, component failure/rejection and software | `layout_metadata`, `region_diagnostics`, provenance JSON and local reopening index |

The owning schema is `dev/schemas/cross-section-drafts.md`. FGDB's naming contract
requires standard names with descriptive variables in tables. The retired loess
support-distance column is not repurposed: new drafts retain typed missing
values and add distinct tangent/boundary-spacing/Chaikin fields. Region-specific
hydraulic calculations, governed identity/acceptance, additions, cross-Reach
collision management and legacy export remain open.

## Verification

Sibling `test_cross_section_regions.R` and `test_cross_section_layout.R` cover
geometry, area/nonoverlap, side labels, containment, artifacts and cut lines.
`test-cross-section-review.R` and `test-cross-section-store.R` cover interaction,
invalidation, identity, metadata and GeoPackage reopening. Scientific acceptance
requires review of actual polygons and centerlines, especially narrow/disconnected
components, branching routes and end caps. The legacy toolbox Centerline
raster-thinning/PAEK code is inspected context and is not copied or invoked.
